Photograph: Reuters First Thing newsletter US news First Thing: Trump promises new Iran talks as Tehran touts Hormuz shipping deal with Oman US president says he called off another US attack on Iran as part of a push for an agreement. Plus why Pokémon Go is still bring global joy 10 years on Martin Belam Mon 3 Aug 2026 07.36 EDT Last modified on Mon 3 Aug 2026 07.58 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Good morning. Donald Trump said talks with Iran would happen on Monday but declined to set a deadline for an agreement, after earlier saying he had called ⁠off an imminent attack. For its part, Iran said it was nearing a deal with Oman over a new route through the strait of Hormuz, and it had no plans to receive a delegation or send an Iranian one to any talks. On Saturday night, Trump claimed on social media that Iran and other Middle Eastern countries had asked for time to complete a deal ⁠that would lead to “the immediate, complete and total” reopening of the strait and “an end to Iran’s nuclear threat”. He added that Tehran must “rapidly make a deal”. What has Iran said about the strait? The Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson, Esmaeil Baqaei, told state television on Sunday that a deal was close with Oman over a new route through the waterway. “We are now going to reach an understanding on a route acceptable to both sides – neither the northern route nor the southern route – but one that respects the sovereign rights of both sides and safeguards our national interests and security,” he said in an interview. RFK Jr tells US families to vaccinate children against measles amid outbreak View image in fullscreen Robert F Kennedy Jr has for years amplified misinformation about vaccines. Photograph: Daniel Heuer/Reuters Robert F Kennedy Jr, the US health secretary, on Sunday told American parents that they should get their children vaccinated against measles , as the surge in infections has reached numbers not seen in the past 35 years. Kennedy, a leading vaccination skeptic who has spent years amplifying misinformation about vaccines, including the shot that protects against measles, mumps and rubella (MMR), made his call in the course of a contentious interview with CNN’s State of the Union on Sunday morning. How many measles cases has the US seen? His remark came as the incidence of measles crossed a milestone – the US has officially recorded 2,371 confirmed infections so far this year, surpassing the total tally in 2025 of 2,289. Taken together, in the past two years there have been more measles infections in the US than in the rest of the 21st century combined. The last time a greater number of measles cases was recorded in a single year was in 1991. Republican calls for Max Miller to resign from Congress after abuse allegations View image in fullscreen Max Miller has denied the allegations against him. Photograph: Jonathan Ernst/Reuters The Republican senator Bernie Moreno on Sunday publicly called for Representative Max Miller, his former son-in-law, to step down from Congress amid allegations of domestic and child abuse. As recently as Friday, the Ohio senator had avoided giving his opinion directly on accusations made by his daughter Emily Moreno against the congressman. The senator’s statement came hours after Miller gave a live stream Sunday morning denying allegations of domestic and child abuse and insisting he would remain in the race for re-election. The public appearance came before Wednesday’s deadline to replace him on the ballot. “Just want to be clear: no court, no agency has ever substantiated any allegation of abuse against me. No criminal charge has ever been filed against me,” Miller said on the live stream. Family to sue after woman released from ICE custody froze to death View image in fullscreen Daphy Michel was found dead at a bus stop. Photograph: Michel family/AP The family of a Haitian immigrant who froze to death in early March at a bus shelter in Pittsburgh after she was dropped off in the city by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is poised to file a lawsuit this month against the US and “multiple other governmental and non-governmental entities”, the Guardian has learned. Daphy Michel, 31, had been in county jail for six months after a reported mental health crisis and street incident, and then was arrested by ICE before being released with an ankle monitor. In other news … View image in fullscreen More than 900 people are battling the Spokane Complex fires. Photograph: Tyler Vanwert via Reuters Eastern Washington fires have destroyed 600 structures and forced 60,000 people to evacuate , stretching the ability of federal and local agencies to fight the blazes. The chaos of a mass border crossing has given way to limbo for Moroccans on the streets of Ceuta , the Spanish colonial enclave in northern Africa. Marcy Kaptur is being treated ⁠for non-life-threatening injuries after a car crash in Toledo, ⁠Ohio, on Sunday, ⁠the ​Democratic US representative’s office said. The suspect in an Idaho restaurant shooting that killed three people died of a self-inflicted gunshot wound , police said. Pressure on the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino, to step down has increased as members of Europe’s footballing authority Uefa prepare to oppose his re-election. Stat of the day: Spider-Man: Brand New Day makes debut to $927m box office View image in fullscreen Tom Holland and Marisa Tomei pose before the Spider-Man: Brand New Day premiere in London. Photograph: Alberto Pezzali/AP The Marvel Studios president, Kevin Feige, has hailed the movie’s “phenomenal” opening – the second biggest opening weekend in history – which followed a box office already buoyed up by The Odyssey and Toy Story 5. Building Power: How free childcare started winning US elections View image in fullscreen The Democratic gubernatorial candidate Francesca Hong. Photograph: Nam Y Huh/AP Sunny Patel reports for the Guardian’s Building Power series on Francesca Hong, a candidate for Wisconsin governor, who is part of a wave of democratic socialists finding traction with an old idea. Don’t miss this: ‘The language of Pokémon is universal’: why fans are still catching ‘em all View image in fullscreen The Pokémon Go character Quaxly in London. Photograph: Niantic/The Pokémon Company/Martin Belam I originally started playing Pokémon Go as a going out activity with my children. Ten years later, they have (mostly) put away childish things, but I still play it every day without fail. In this lovely piece , Sammy Gecsoyler speaks to devoted players who explain how the game has created a vibrant intergenerational community spanning the globe. … or this: Hide the Pain Harold and Rubik’s Cube creator among social media’s picks for Hungarian president View image in fullscreen Péter Magyar, the Hungarian prime minister. Photograph: Robert Hegedus/MTI/AP Péter Magyar and his newly elected Tisza party asked the public to put forward names for the next president of Hungary, which is resetting its politics after years of being dominated by the rightwing populist Viktor Orbán. The suggestions have ranged from the sensible to the downright bizarre . Climate check: ‘Stop all outdoor activities’ – South Korea records its highest ever temperature View image in fullscreen Children play at a fountain to cool down during a heatwave warning in Seoul. Photograph: Kim Hong-Ji/Reuters South Korea has registered its highest temperature since records began more than a century ago, at 42.5C, as authorities warned people to immediately stop all outdoor activities in affected areas. London’s Kew Gardens has gone without rain for a whole month for the first time in history, as Europe continues to battle a heatwave. Two firefighting helicopters have collided west of Athens , killing the two-person crew of one of the aircraft, as efforts to control a massive wildfire barrelling towards the outskirts of the Greek capital intensified. Last Thing: ‘The greatest arms I’ve ever seen’: Matt Damon’s muscular female stunt double Devyn Dalton View image in fullscreen Devyn Dalton standing in for Matt Damon on a poster for The Odyssey. Photograph: Landmark Media/Alamy A 35-year-old stuntwoman is one of the great unsung heroes of Christopher Nolan’s new blockbuster The Odyssey – standing in for Matt Damon and displaying what the actor called “the greatest arms I’ve ever seen”. Canadian Devyn Dalton was the Hollywood star’s stunt double in a pivotal scene. Olivia Bowden spoke to her . https://www.dw.com/en/yemen-houthis-take.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5MOu4 The port city of Mokha lies near the crucial Bab el-Mandeb strait [FILE: August 10, 2026] Image: Al Joumhouriya TV/Handout/REUTERS Advertisement Yemen's Houthi militia captured the port city of Mokha (also spelled Mocha) on Thursday, sparking fears the country could return to civil war . The city lies around 80 kilometers (50 miles) from the Bab el-Mandeb strait, an important waterway for shipping that divides the Red Sea from the Gulf of Aden. The Red Sea has served as a key alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where shipping has been disrupted amid the United States' war with Iran , sending global oil prices skyrocketing. Houthi spokesperson Abdulsalam was cited by the Reuters news agency as saying that freedom of navigation and international trade in the Red Sea and the Strait remain safe and operations are limited to specific targets. The Houthis have in the past targeted international shipping in the Red Sea, saying it is in solidarity with Palestinians in Gaza. Meanwhile, Houthi rebels accused Saudi Arabia of launching strikes on the southwestern province of Taiz. "The Saudi enemy launched 10 strikes on the Dhubab district in western Taiz," the Houthis' Al-Masirah TV channel was cited by AFP news agency as saying. Dhubab lies just south of Mokha. For a long time, Mokha had been held by forces aligned with Yemen's internationally recognized government [FILE: September 2021] Image: Planet Labs Inc./AP Photo/picture alliance Fighting intensifies between Houthis and Yemeni government Fighting has intensified between the Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognized government in recent months after four years of relative calm, with rebels intensifying efforts to solidify their control over the country's coastline. The capture of Mokha is the Iran-backed militia's biggest territorial gain since a UN-brokered truce signed in 2022 . The Iran-backed Houthis control the Yemeni capital, Sanaa, as well as much of the more populous areas in the country's north and west. The internationally recognized government has its headquarters in the southern city of Aden and receives considerable support from Saudi Arabia. Yemen's civil war has killed over 150,000 people and brought others to the brink of famine.
